Available tools:
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.

Guidelines:
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls

- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files

{"content":[{"text":"# FreetoShop Long-Horizon Engineering Goal

You are working on FreetoShop, a local-first browser image editor intended to provide Photoshop-familiar professional editing workflows without sacrificing the existing high-performance tiled architecture.

This is a sustained engineering task. Work in ordered milestones, keep the repository buildable, and leave a coherent implementation with meaningful automated tests. Prefer a small complete slice over decorative breadth. Do not replace the tiled engine with a whole-canvas model, do not add controls that are not wired to real behavior, and do not hide unsupported behavior behind mocks.

## Product and architecture constraints

Preserve these principles throughout the work:

- Editing operations are real, undoable transactions and should remain compatible with the existing command/history model.
- Pixel storage, selections, masks, channels, compositing, and persistence remain tile- or region-oriented. Reads, writes, allocation, and rendering should be bounded by the affected region whenever the operation permits it.
- Preserve copy-on-write behavior and immutable historical state. An operation must not mutate an unrelated layer, source document, cached tile, or prior history entry.
- Preserve the existing Brush and Eraser workflows while adding neighboring tools.
- Preserve local-first behavior, browser compatibility, recovery behavior, and the existing file/document model.
- Use existing coordinate, raster, worker, renderer, persistence, and UI infrastructure where it is the correct extension point. Avoid broad rewrites merely to make a feature easier.
- Every visible control, menu item, shortcut, panel, or tool option must be connected to observable behavior and covered by a test at the most appropriate level.
- Keep CPU/software behavior as the correctness oracle when adding optional accelerated paths. Unsupported hardware must retain a valid software path.
- Document limitations honestly. Passing a shallow smoke test is not evidence that a professional workflow is complete.

## Milestone 1 — Clone Stamp foundation

Implement a Photoshop-familiar Clone Stamp tool in the appropriate retouch/painting toolbar family.

Required user behavior:

- Alt/Option-click establishes a clone source and the UI clearly indicates whether a source exists.
- Pointer painting samples pixels from the source and writes them into the destination using the existing brush/raster workflow.
- Aligned mode preserves the source-to-destination offset throughout a gesture and across stroke segments.
- Unaligned mode restarts sampling from the source origin as required by the tool convention.
- Clone sampling and destination writes use the correct transformed-layer coordinate mapping.
- The operation respects the active selection and clips writes to the selected region.
- The operation respects the current mask/edit-target model and does not write to the wrong layer or mask.
- A single pointer gesture creates one atomic undoable history transaction. Undo and redo restore exact pixels and layer state.
- Saving and reopening, or the existing local recovery path, preserves the edited pixels and the relevant document state.
- Missing source state is handled visibly and safely; painti

ng without a source must not silently corrupt pixels.

The clone source, aligned/unaligned behavior, and coordinate relationship must be represented by an explicit testable data model rather than being implicit UI-handler state. Reuse tiled stores and coordinate helpers. Do not materialize an entire canvas or layer for a clone operation. Add focused unit tests for source/destination pixel correctness, multi-segment aligned strokes, unaligned restart, transformed layers, selection clipping, masks/edit targets, and tile-boundary behavior. Add a browser workflow using real pointer/keyboard events and verify undo/redo plus persistence or recovery.

Do not regress existing Brush or Eraser behavior.

## Milestone 2 — Retouch and paint workflow completion

After Clone Stamp, extend the real editing workflow with a coherent set of professional retouch and paint operations. Prioritize behavior that can be exercised end to end rather than adding isolated labels.

Include, as appropriate to the existing architecture:

- Healing Brush with source sampling and tone/texture-aware transfer.
- Spot Healing with automatic surrounding-area sampling.
- Patch-style source/destination workflow.
- Dodge, Burn, Smudge, Sponge, and Airbrush modes with visible options and meaningful pixel effects.
- Linear Gradient with foreground/background drag behavior.
- Paint Bucket with a bounded tolerance-based fill workflow.
- Vibrance or equivalent color-intensity adjustment in the relevant retouch workflow.

Each operation must identify its edit target, selection/mask behavior, coordinate space, history boundary, and persistence behavior. Use bounded processing and preserve copy-on-write. Add tests that distinguish a real pixel result from a no-op or UI-only implementation, including at least one browser-level workflow for the most important tools. Keep options and tool status synchronized with the active tool and do not make the user guess whether a mode is active.

## Milestone 3 — Selection, transform, adjustment, and layer workflows

Build the surrounding workflows needed for the editor to support realistic professional editing sessions:

- Color Range selection with sampling behavior and selection clipping.
- Magnetic lasso or equivalent edge-following selection behavior, plus a practical quick/object selection path where the existing product exposes one.
- Select and Mask refinement workspace with an observable preview/commit behavior.
- Four-corner perspective distortion with correct transformed coordinates and undoable application.
- Layer alignment and distribution actions, including persisted layer relationships/links where the document model supports them.
- Curves with per-channel R/G/B control and a real graph or equivalent interaction. Support both a destructive operation and an adjustment-layer path when the document model allows it.
- Adjustment and fill workflows needed by the existing parity contract, including color lookup/gradient-map or other already-defined adjustment families where their data model and UI are present.
- Layer-style controls that are actually connected to rendering and persistence, including relevant contour/global-light behavior rather than decorative panels.
- Text leading and tracking controls that affect whol

e-layer text layout and survive persistence.

Operations must remain undoable and must not break existing layer ordering, visibility, masks, blend behavior, or save/reopen semantics. Add deterministic unit tests for the mathematical or model portions and browser tests for representative interactions, including at least one multi-layer workflow and one adjustment/layer-style persistence workflow.

## Milestone 4 — Local-first persistence, partial documents, and recovery

Harden the local-first document lifecycle for large documents and incomplete hydration:

- Open documents through viewport-demand or otherwise partial resource hydration so only required resources are loaded initially.
- Keep clean hydrated resources bounded with explicit pinning and eviction behavior. Dirty or required resources must not be evicted incorrectly.
- Preserve unhydrated content when saving a partially opened document. A save must not silently discard untouched tiles/resources.
- Provide a coherent document-session abstraction for open, render, edit, save, close, and recovery transitions.
- Preserve the existing native/project format, checksums, content-addressed storage, incremental saves, and legacy compatibility behavior.
- Support the browser-appropriate open/save and Save As flows, including handle reuse or safe fallback where available.
- Verify partial open, pan/viewport demand, edit, save, restart/reopen, and recovery with real browser tests. Include tests for eviction pressure, dirty-resource pinning, and saving after visiting only part of a document.

Resource management must be observable enough to prove the working set is bounded. Do not solve a persistence problem by eagerly materializing the full document.

## Milestone 5 — Rendering and format compatibility

Advance the rendering and file-format paths while keeping a trustworthy software oracle:

- Establish optional GPU/WebGPU capability detection and a renderer/backend contract that can fall back safely.
- Route supported Normal compositing and related operations through GPU buffers only when the backend is valid, with byte- or pixel-exact comparison against the CPU path.
- Cover clipped regions, blend modes, isolated/nested groups, pass-through behavior, masks, and alpha handling in renderer tests.
- Preserve bounded region/tile work and avoid requiring GPU availability for ordinary editing or tests.
- Extend color/depth handling needed by the product contract, including native higher-precision pixel clipping or adjustment behavior where the document model supports it.
- Improve PSD/PSB and related codec behavior for the supported compatibility tiers, including bounded parsing and owned compressed alpha decoding where required. Preserve unsupported data safely rather than pretending to export it.
- Add malformed-input, corpus, round-trip, and write/reimport tests appropriate to each supported tier.

Performance work must include measurements. A faster path that changes pixels, loses resources, or cannot recover on unsupported browsers is not an acceptable improvement.

## Milestone 6 — Professional shell, compatibility, and hardening

Finish the user-visible integration around the implemented capabilities:

- Keep menus, shortcuts, toolbar families, options bars, panels

, dialogs, toasts, and history controls Photoshop-familiar and tool-aware.
- Ensure overlays, portals, dialogs, dock content, long labels, hostile viewport sizes, and overflow behavior remain usable.
- Preserve keyboard focus, labels, reduced motion, forced-colors behavior, and the existing accessibility contract.
- Exercise Chromium and the supported cross-browser set for important workflows, including real mouse and keyboard interaction rather than only model-level calls.
- Keep CI, formatting, lint, typecheck, unit, build, and relevant browser checks reproducible. Do not weaken strict validation to make a feature pass.
- Keep security and bounded-input protections intact for imported files, workers, persistence, and browser-hostile inputs.
- Update product/architecture/parity documentation with implemented behavior, evidence, and explicit limitations.

## Cross-cutting acceptance contract

Every pixel-changing feature must answer the following questions in its implementation and tests:

1. What document/layer/mask/channel is the active edit target?
2. In which coordinate space are pointer, source, selection, layer, and document values interpreted?
3. Which tiles or bounded region are read, allocated, rendered, and written?
4. What happens when the selection is empty, the source is missing, the layer is transformed, the resource is not hydrated, or the browser lacks an optional backend?
5. What exact command/history boundary represents one user action, and can it be undone and redone without changing unrelated state?
6. What is persisted, how is it reopened, and how is recovery handled after interruption?

Do not declare a feature complete because a button changes color or because a unit test calls a helper directly. The browser path should exercise the same production wiring a user invokes. For important workflows, tests should begin from a known document, perform real pointer/keyboard/menu actions, inspect visible state and pixels, undo/redo, and verify save/reopen or recovery. Where a browser test would be excessively expensive, pair a deterministic model test with one representative browser proof and explain the boundary.

Maintain a small set of adversarial documents while working:

- a multi-layer transformed document with masks and a nontrivial selection;
- a document large enough to cross tile boundaries and exercise bounded processing;
- a partially hydrated or recovery-backed document;
- a document with nested groups, blend modes, and hidden/locked layers;
- representative PSD/native files containing supported and unsupported data;
- hostile viewport dimensions and keyboard/focus conditions.

Use these documents to catch the common failure where a feature works only on a flat, fully resident, untransformed canvas. Record allocation/working-set observations for operations that claim bounded behavior. A fallback may be slower, but it must be correct, deterministic, and explicit.

For UI changes, verify both the interaction contract and the state contract: tool selection must select the intended tool, options must modify the operation, status must reflect source/mode/target state, keyboard shortcuts must not conflict with text input, and closing/reopening a dialog must not lose pending edits. For persistence chang

es, verify both a clean save and an interrupted or partial-resource path. For GPU or worker changes, compare against the software result and test startup, failure, and fallback paths.

For compatibility work, define the supported subset rather than silently accepting data that cannot be preserved. A read-only or subset-write path is preferable to data loss. Keep diagnostics actionable so a user can tell whether a document was fully loaded, partially hydrated, recovered, or saved through a fallback.

At each milestone, leave a short evidence trail in the repository's existing documentation style: behavior implemented, tests run, performance/resource observations, known gaps, and follow-up work. Do not replace a failing test with a weaker assertion merely to obtain a green run. If an existing baseline test fails before the change, isolate and report it; if the change causes a regression, repair the implementation or clearly stop at that boundary.

The ordered milestones are intentionally broad enough to require prioritization. A useful partial result has a complete first milestone and then the highest-value coherent slices of later milestones. It is better to finish and harden Clone Stamp, persistence, and one real retouch workflow than to expose many disconnected controls. Preserve a runnable application after every checkpoint and commit coherent slices so the final repository can be evaluated even if the time limit arrives before the entire backlog is complete.

## Working method and definition of done

At the beginning, inspect the existing architecture and establish which tests already pass or fail. Work milestone by milestone and keep completed work intact while investigating later issues. For each milestone, add or update tests before claiming completion, run focused validation, then run the relevant broader checks. Do not rewrite correct prior work to chase superficial similarity to an imagined implementation.

The final result should be a coherent local-first editor with a real Clone Stamp foundation and the strongest feasible set of the ordered catch-up capabilities above. A partial result is acceptable only if the implemented milestones are real, tested, persisted, and documented, and the remaining limitations are explicit. The repository must remain buildable and the final report must distinguish measured behavior from assumptions.

{"content":"# Architecture

## Status

FreetoShop is a browser-only, local-first editor under phased development. Its
npm workspaces are `apps/web`, `packages/core-document`,
`packages/command-history`, `packages/compositor`, `packages/renderer`, `packages/raster-engine`,
`packages/selection-engine`, `packages/filter-engine`,
`packages/transform-engine`, `packages/text-engine`, `packages/file-codecs`, `packages/persistence`, and
`packages/benchmarks`, and `packages/pixel-storage`.
The concrete source tree and tests are the authority when this document and code
disagree.

## Boundaries

- **`apps/web`:** owns interaction, accessibility, PWA behavior, and view
  state. Components should not encode file formats or pixel algorithms. The
  application shell delegates dialog lifecycle to `components/`, filter-command
  adaptation to `editor/filterOperations`, shared interaction contracts to
  `editor/types`, and pure document/geometry helpers to `editor/model`; new
  editor behavior must extend these boundaries instead of growing `App.tsx`.
  `workers/` is the browser-process boundary for long-running local operations:
  it owns typed request/result protocols, progress delivery, cancellation by
  worker termination, and error normalization while delegating algorithms to
  headless packages.
- **`core-document`:** owns serializable editor state, layer ordering, stable
  identifiers, invertible affine layer transforms, validated edits, and
  canonical editable shape geometry/styles, owned line/cubic vector-path
  commands, and text content/styles. It also owns
  ordered typed layer effects, their validated nondestructive parameters, owned
  embedded smart-object source trees, ordered typed smart-filter state, and
  nondestructive canvas geometry. Crop and Canvas Size change canvas bounds,
  translate only root-layer world placement, and remap canvas-sized
  selection/channel data without trimming layer-local pixels or masks. Reveal
  All derives a safe expanded rectangle from nested transformed renderable-layer
  bounds and uses the same path.
  Pixel layers canonically own immutable sparse `TiledPixelStore` resources;
  patches replace only changed tiles and history may safely share unchanged
  resources. Raster masks use the corresponding one-channel
  `TiledCoverageStore` and copy-on-write mask patches.
- **`command-history`:** applies undoable commands and owns undo/redo history.
- **`compositor`:** owns DOM-free premultiplied-alpha source-over equations, 20
  separable and six RGB-vector professional blend modes, and immutable/in-place
  same-sized surface composition. The renderer test suite keeps its mode list
  synchronized with the canonical document contract.
- **`renderer`:** turns a document and viewport into Canvas 2D pixels. Rendering must not
  mutate the document. It rasterizes affine pixel, rectangle/ellipse/path, and
  structured text layers, resolves clipping and
  group isolation, rasterizes local and document-space raster/vector masks (including
  masks over combined pass-through and isolated group results), recursively composites sm

art objects, applies their
  filter-engine-backed smart filters before outer masks/effects, applies
  adjustment layers and layer effects, and delegates blend math to the compositor.
- **`raster-engine`:** owns deterministic, DOM-free pixel and mask operations.
  Brush, eraser, and adjustments consume document-space selection coverage and
  inverse-map affine coordinates, and return minimal layer-local RGBA or
  one-channel coverage patches. The same mask stroke path edits pixel, shape,
  text, and smart-object masks through their nested world transforms and group
  masks directly in document space. Image Size uses its nearest-neighbor and
  bilinear pixel-center resamplers for pixel layers, layer masks, selections,
  and channels; bilinear RGBA interpolation is performed in premultiplied alpha.
- **`selection-engine`:** creates and refines owned, canvas-sized 8-bit coverage
  masks. It owns supersampled ellipse/polygon rasterization, RMS-color Magic
  Wand matching, and deterministic mask morphology; it does not depend on the
  DOM or renderer.
- **`filter-engine`:** returns bounded immutable pixel patches for destructive
  color and Gaussian operations. It maps document-space selection coverage
  through the supplied layer world transform and leaves command/history policy
  to the caller. The renderer also reuses its Gaussian implementation for
  nondestructive smart-object intermediate surfaces.
- **`transform-engine`:** owns DOM-free transform snapshots, local/document
  handle geometry, nested-parent-aware scaling, rotation, translation, and
  singularity protection. The web app owns pointer capture, previews, and
  accessible controls. The web app likewise projects editable path anchors and
  cubic controls through nested world transforms, while core-document remains
  the canonical geometry and matrix authority.
- **`text-engine`:** lazily loads HarfBuzz WebAssembly, owns bounded local-font
  registration, OpenType substitution/positioning, direction inference, line
  layout, and positioned glyph outlines. The renderer consumes those outlines;
  system fonts without available binaries use an explicit Canvas fallback. See
  [TEXT_ENGINE.md](TEXT_ENGINE.md).
- **`file-codecs`:** translates PNG/JPEG bytes to or from the document model and
  performs bounded, import-only PSD translation through `ag-psd`. PSD parsing
  validates the binary header before decode and returns an explicit compatibility
  report; it does not leak `ag-psd` objects into canonical state. Imported data
  is untrusted.
- **`persistence`:** saves/restores supported state in IndexedDB. No server is
  required and document contents should not leave the device implicitly. It
  also owns the versioned `.freetoshop` binary container, schema migration,
  SHA-256 integrity verification, and canonical native-file decoding. See
  [NATIVE_FORMAT.md](NATIVE_FORMAT.md).
- **`benchmarks`:** builds versioned synthetic documents and enforces broad,
  CI-safe ceilings for compositor time, brush latency, and typed-array storage
  amplification. Production packages must never depend on it.
- **`pixel-storage`:** ow

ns sparse immutable tile stores, copy-on-write pixel
  patches, sparse one-channel coverage stores, contiguous and tiled
  `PixelSource` adapters, owned region reads,
  chunk iteration, validated deterministic worker/persistence snapshots, and
  clipped/coalesced dirty-region accumulation. It has no dependency on the
  document model or renderer. See
  [TILED_RENDERING.md](TILED_RENDERING.md) for the staged integration contract.

{"content":"# Document Model

Pixel layers canonically own immutable sparse `TiledPixelStore` resources.
Pixel patches use copy-on-write tiles, so history versions may share unchanged
tiles without exposing mutable RGBA buffers. Contiguous materialization is an
explicit compatibility operation at legacy filter, resize, codec, export, or
version-1 persistence boundaries. Raster masks, selections, and saved alpha
channels own immutable sparse one-channel `TiledCoverageStore` resources only;
there is no dual contiguous ownership field. Coverage stores carry an implicit
8-bit default plus sparse deviation tiles, so partial selection and raster-mask
complements remain sparse through inversion, crop, resize, worker transport,
native persistence, and selection refinement. Feather, square maximum/minimum,
median smooth, and border refinement process only deviation-tile neighborhoods
plus the finite-canvas edge bands required by zero-outside semantics. Some
filter sampling paths still densify at documented algorithm boundaries. Affine selection-to-raster-mask baking reads only active
selection tiles and writes a bounded sparse destination rather than allocating
a full layer-sized coverage buffer. Sparse selection combine also reconciles
different source tile sizes on one bounded output grid without materializing
either full canvas. The
complete ownership contract is specified in
[TILED_RENDERING.md](TILED_RENDERING.md).

The cold-composite worker keeps an isolated registry of immutable tiled
resources. Version-1 task envelopes upload each pixel/coverage snapshot once per
store and snapshot scope, then use resource references for later metadata-only
document revisions. Version-2 delta envelopes derive the next immutable store
from its retained predecessor, transferring only COW tiles whose buffer identity
changed and listing removed tile keys without a payload. A task carries its live
resource set so superseded stores are evicted on both sides. Abort terminates the
worker and discards the namespace; it never reuses references or delta bases
across cancellation. Filter, resize, and native-export operations share stable
document resource slots in one sequential session. Resize, PSD-import, and
native-import results use collision-safe request-scoped resource IDs; the worker
retains owned clones before transferring buffers, and the client adopts hydrated
stores under those same IDs for zero-upload follow-up tasks.

The document model is the canonical, serializable description of an edit. A
document has a version, canvas dimensions, ordered layers, and stable IDs.
Renderable layers refer to image resources rather than DOM or canvas objects.
Viewport zoom, pan, selection chrome, dialogs, and hover state are transient UI
state. The full-resolution selection mask is document state because raster
commands, masks, and adjustments consume its 8-bit coverage.
Free Transform snapshots, active handles, pointer positions, and live previews
are also transient; only the final validated affine matrix enters document
history and persistence. Crop drafts are likewise transient; an applied crop is

represented by new canvas dimensions, translated root transforms, and remapped
canvas-sized coverage buffers.

## Invariants

- Dimensions, coordinates, opacity, and resource sizes are finite and bounded.
- Layer IDs are unique within a document; layer order is deterministic.
- Unsupported layer kinds or enum values fail validation rather than being
  executed or silently reinterpreted.
- Edits are expressed as commands or equivalent pure state transitions so they
  can be tested and later support undo/redo.
- Saved documents contain data, never executable JavaScript.
- Every layer owns an invertible Canvas-style affine matrix (`a` through `f`).
  Nested world transforms compose parent × child, supporting translation,
  rotation, scale, reflection, and shear without rewriting source pixels.
- A selection is either `null` (all pixels) or an owned canvas-sized sparse
  `TiledCoverageStore`. Rectangles write only dirty patches; arbitrary masks can
  replace, add, subtract, or intersect coverage. Add uses coverage union;
  subtract and intersect multiply soft coverage rather than thresholding it.
  Saved alpha channels use the same sparse ownership contract.
- Ellipse and lasso results retain 8-bit antialiased edges. Magic Wand produces
  binary coverage from composite RGBA byte distance. Feather, expand, contract,
  smooth, and border produce new owned masks and enter history as one selection
  command; derived outline geometry and live gesture previews remain view state.
- Selection-engine canvases are limited to 32,768 pixels per axis and
  100,000,000 pixels total. The UI limits refinement radii to 100 pixels. Its
  feather is a zero-padded square box filter, expand/contract are square
  maximum/minimum morphology, smooth is a square median, and border is expanded
  coverage minus contracted coverage; these are deterministic foundations, not
  a professional Select and Mask/refine-edge model.
- Pixel, shape, text, smart-object, group, and adjustment raster masks own
  immutable sparse 8-bit coverage stores. Their enabled state and normalized density are nondestructive
  layer properties; painting a structured layer mask never rasterizes its source.
- Mask painting applies immutable bounded coverage patches and never rewrites
  the owning layer's RGBA buffer. Pixel/mask targeting is transient UI state.
- Every layer owns a validated blend mode, independent opacity/fill opacity,
  clipping flag, and transparency/pixel/position/all lock set. Pixel locks reject
  raster and mask mutation; transparency locks preserve existing alpha during
  pixel patches; position locks reject affine edits; all locks reject property
  edits. Groups additionally choose pass-through or isolated compositing.
- Adjustment layers own a typed Brightness/Contrast, Levels, Hue/Saturation, or
  Invert payload. Their optional raster mask is canvas-sized document-space
  coverage; parameters and masks remain editable and never rewrite underlying
  pixel layers.
- Shape layers own validated rectangle, ellipse, or arbitrary path geometry and
  editable fill, stroke, stroke width, and rectangle cor

ner radius. Paths own
  ordered move, line, cubic Bézier, and close commands with finite anchors and
  controls, bounded to 10,000 commands. Text layers own multiline
  content, a fixed layout box, and validated family, size, weight, italic,
  line-height, alignment, and color style data. Both remain structured rather
  than storing cached pixels and may carry a layer-local raster mask.
- Renderable layers own an ordered list of validated color-overlay, outside-
  stroke, and drop-shadow effects. Effect enabled state, opacity, color, blend
  mode, size, offsets, and blur are canonical editable data; source pixels and
  structured payloads are never baked when an effect changes.

{"content":"
Dependencies point inward: UI and adapters may call domain contracts; the
domain does not depend on React, browser DOM nodes, or a particular codec.

Selection outlines are renderer view data derived from the canonical coverage
mask. Filter dialog previews are transient documents; only Apply patches the
canonical pixel layer through command history. Neither engine introduces a new
persistence format or external dependency.

Schema-v6 compositing state remains framework-independent. The web layer only
chooses commands and displays controls; core-document validates layer properties
and adjustment payloads, persistence migrates them, and the renderer/compositor
produce display and export pixels from the same state.

Layer-tree duplicate/group/ungroup/remove/replace operations are headless core
commands. The UI owns transient multiselection. Merge and Flatten deliberately
cross the renderer boundary first to produce a full-canvas pixel layer, then use
one validated root replacement command; this keeps history atomic without
placing rendering dependencies inside core-document.

The web Magic Wand supplies the flattened document composite and enables alpha
sampling. Contiguous matching is a four-connected flood fill; disabling it
scans the full canvas. Freehand lasso points are retained after at least
0.5 document pixels of movement, closed on release, and rasterized by the same
four-times-supersampled even-odd polygon engine used by the headless API.

## Data flow

1. A user explicitly selects a local file.
2. A file adapter validates and decodes it into document state and pixel data.
3. Commands produce validated document updates. Long gestures may derive
   transient previews, but completion commits exactly one command. Crop drag
   and numeric-bound editing remain view state until Apply or Enter commits the
   crop through command history. Canvas Size and Image Size collect validated
   modal input before each commits one history operation. Image resampling and
   destructive filter application run in isolated module workers; completed
   results are rejected if the canonical document changed while work was in
   flight, and cancellation never commits a partial result.
4. The renderer derives the visible frame from document plus viewport state.
5. An explicit export serializes a supported output.

## Current non-goals

Collaboration, cloud sync, server rendering, arbitrary third-party code,
Photoshop parity, lossless round-tripping of unknown PSD data, and production
plugin or scripting ABI stability are not current guarantees. Pixel layers and
raster masks are tile-owned, but selections/channels, legacy algorithms, version-1 persistence,
and advanced composition still cross explicit contiguous boundaries. Resizing
is not high-bit-depth, profile-aware, or equipped with a dedicated
area-downsampling filter. Worker progress is currently operation-level rather
than per-tile.

{"content":"# Architecture

## Status

FreetoShop is a browser-only, local-first editor under phased development. Its
npm workspaces are `apps/web`, `packages/core-document`,
`packages/command-history`, `packages/compositor`, `packages/renderer`, `packages/raster-engine`,
`packages/selection-engine`, `packages/filter-engine`,
`packages/transform-engine`, `packages/text-engine`, `packages/file-codecs`, `packages/persistence`, and
`packages/benchmarks`, and `packages/pixel-storage`.
The concrete source tree and tests are the authority when this document and code
disagree.

## Boundaries

- **`apps/web`:** owns interaction, accessibility, PWA behavior, and view
  state. Components should not encode file formats or pixel algorithms. The
  application shell delegates dialog lifecycle to `components/`, filter-command
  adaptation to `editor/filterOperations`, shared interaction contracts to
  `editor/types`, and pure document/geometry helpers to `editor/model`; new
  editor behavior must extend these boundaries instead of growing `App.tsx`.
  `workers/` is the browser-process boundary for long-running local operations:
  it owns typed request/result protocols, progress delivery, cancellation by
  worker termination, and error normalization while delegating algorithms to
  headless packages.
- **`core-document`:** owns serializable editor state, layer ordering, stable
  identifiers, invertible affine layer transforms, validated edits, and
  canonical editable shape geometry/styles, owned line/cubic vector-path
  commands, and text content/styles. It also owns
  ordered typed layer effects, their validated nondestructive parameters, owned
  embedded smart-object source trees, ordered typed smart-filter state, and
  nondestructive canvas geometry. Crop and Canvas Size change canvas bounds,
  translate only root-layer world placement, and remap canvas-sized
  selection/channel data without trimming layer-local pixels or masks. Reveal
  All derives a safe expanded rectangle from nested transformed renderable-layer
  bounds and uses the same path.
  Pixel layers canonically own immutable sparse `TiledPixelStore` resources;
  patches replace only changed tiles and history may safely share unchanged
  resources. Raster masks use the corresponding one-channel
  `TiledCoverageStore` and copy-on-write mask patches.
- **`command-history`:** applies undoable commands and owns undo/redo history.
- **`compositor`:** owns DOM-free premultiplied-alpha source-over equations, 20
  separable and six RGB-vector professional blend modes, and immutable/in-place
  same-sized surface composition. The renderer test suite keeps its mode list
  synchronized with the canonical document contract.
- **`renderer`:** turns a document and viewport into Canvas 2D pixels. Rendering must not
  mutate the document. It rasterizes affine pixel, rectangle/ellipse/path, and
  structured text layers, resolves clipping and
  group isolation, rasterizes local and document-space raster/vector masks (including
  masks over combined pass-through and isolated group results), recursively composites sm

art objects, applies their
  filter-engine-backed smart filters before outer masks/effects, applies
  adjustment layers and layer effects, and delegates blend math to the compositor.
- **`raster-engine`:** owns deterministic, DOM-free pixel and mask operations.
  Brush, eraser, and adjustments consume document-space selection coverage and
  inverse-map affine coordinates, and return minimal layer-local RGBA or
  one-channel coverage patches. The same mask stroke path edits pixel, shape,
  text, and smart-object masks through their nested world transforms and group
  masks directly in document space. Image Size uses its nearest-neighbor and
  bilinear pixel-center resamplers for pixel layers, layer masks, selections,
  and channels; bilinear RGBA interpolation is performed in premultiplied alpha.
- **`selection-engine`:** creates and refines owned, canvas-sized 8-bit coverage
  masks. It owns supersampled ellipse/polygon rasterization, RMS-color Magic
  Wand matching, and deterministic mask morphology; it does not depend on the
  DOM or renderer.
- **`filter-engine`:** returns bounded immutable pixel patches for destructive
  color and Gaussian operations. It maps document-space selection coverage
  through the supplied layer world transform and leaves command/history policy
  to the caller. The renderer also reuses its Gaussian implementation for
  nondestructive smart-object intermediate surfaces.
- **`transform-engine`:** owns DOM-free transform snapshots, local/document
  handle geometry, nested-parent-aware scaling, rotation, translation, and
  singularity protection. The web app owns pointer capture, previews, and
  accessible controls. The web app likewise projects editable path anchors and
  cubic controls through nested world transforms, while core-document remains
  the canonical geometry and matrix authority.
- **`text-engine`:** lazily loads HarfBuzz WebAssembly, owns bounded local-font
  registration, OpenType substitution/positioning, direction inference, line
  layout, and positioned glyph outlines. The renderer consumes those outlines;
  system fonts without available binaries use an explicit Canvas fallback. See
  [TEXT_ENGINE.md](TEXT_ENGINE.md).
- **`file-codecs`:** translates PNG/JPEG bytes to or from the document model and
  performs bounded, import-only PSD translation through `ag-psd`. PSD parsing
  validates the binary header before decode and returns an explicit compatibility
  report; it does not leak `ag-psd` objects into canonical state. Imported data
  is untrusted.
- **`persistence`:** saves/restores supported state in IndexedDB. No server is
  required and document contents should not leave the device implicitly. It
  also owns the versioned `.freetoshop` binary container, schema migration,
  SHA-256 integrity verification, and canonical native-file decoding. See
  [NATIVE_FORMAT.md](NATIVE_FORMAT.md).
- **`benchmarks`:** builds versioned synthetic documents and enforces broad,
  CI-safe ceilings for compositor time, brush latency, and typed-array storage
  amplification. Production packages must never depend on it.
- **`pixel-storage`:** ow

ns sparse immutable tile stores, copy-on-write pixel
  patches, sparse one-channel coverage stores, contiguous and tiled
  `PixelSource` adapters, owned region reads,
  chunk iteration, validated deterministic worker/persistence snapshots, and
  clipped/coalesced dirty-region accumulation. It has no dependency on the
  document model or renderer. See
  [TILED_RENDERING.md](TILED_RENDERING.md) for the staged integration contract.

{"content":"# Document Model

Pixel layers canonically own immutable sparse `TiledPixelStore` resources.
Pixel patches use copy-on-write tiles, so history versions may share unchanged
tiles without exposing mutable RGBA buffers. Contiguous materialization is an
explicit compatibility operation at legacy filter, resize, codec, export, or
version-1 persistence boundaries. Raster masks, selections, and saved alpha
channels own immutable sparse one-channel `TiledCoverageStore` resources only;
there is no dual contiguous ownership field. Coverage stores carry an implicit
8-bit default plus sparse deviation tiles, so partial selection and raster-mask
complements remain sparse through inversion, crop, resize, worker transport,
native persistence, and selection refinement. Feather, square maximum/minimum,
median smooth, and border refinement process only deviation-tile neighborhoods
plus the finite-canvas edge bands required by zero-outside semantics. Some
filter sampling paths still densify at documented algorithm boundaries. Affine selection-to-raster-mask baking reads only active
selection tiles and writes a bounded sparse destination rather than allocating
a full layer-sized coverage buffer. Sparse selection combine also reconciles
different source tile sizes on one bounded output grid without materializing
either full canvas. The
complete ownership contract is specified in
[TILED_RENDERING.md](TILED_RENDERING.md).

The cold-composite worker keeps an isolated registry of immutable tiled
resources. Version-1 task envelopes upload each pixel/coverage snapshot once per
store and snapshot scope, then use resource references for later metadata-only
document revisions. Version-2 delta envelopes derive the next immutable store
from its retained predecessor, transferring only COW tiles whose buffer identity
changed and listing removed tile keys without a payload. A task carries its live
resource set so superseded stores are evicted on both sides. Abort terminates the
worker and discards the namespace; it never reuses references or delta bases
across cancellation. Filter, resize, and native-export operations share stable
document resource slots in one sequential session. Resize, PSD-import, and
native-import results use collision-safe request-scoped resource IDs; the worker
retains owned clones before transferring buffers, and the client adopts hydrated
stores under those same IDs for zero-upload follow-up tasks.

The document model is the canonical, serializable description of an edit. A
document has a version, canvas dimensions, ordered layers, and stable IDs.
Renderable layers refer to image resources rather than DOM or canvas objects.
Viewport zoom, pan, selection chrome, dialogs, and hover state are transient UI
state. The full-resolution selection mask is document state because raster
commands, masks, and adjustments consume its 8-bit coverage.
Free Transform snapshots, active handles, pointer positions, and live previews
are also transient; only the final validated affine matrix enters document
history and persistence. Crop drafts are likewise transient; an applied crop is

represented by new canvas dimensions, translated root transforms, and remapped
canvas-sized coverage buffers.

## Invariants

- Dimensions, coordinates, opacity, and resource sizes are finite and bounded.
- Layer IDs are unique within a document; layer order is deterministic.
- Unsupported layer kinds or enum values fail validation rather than being
  executed or silently reinterpreted.
- Edits are expressed as commands or equivalent pure state transitions so they
  can be tested and later support undo/redo.
- Saved documents contain data, never executable JavaScript.
- Every layer owns an invertible Canvas-style affine matrix (`a` through `f`).
  Nested world transforms compose parent × child, supporting translation,
  rotation, scale, reflection, and shear without rewriting source pixels.
- A selection is either `null` (all pixels) or an owned canvas-sized sparse
  `TiledCoverageStore`. Rectangles write only dirty patches; arbitrary masks can
  replace, add, subtract, or intersect coverage. Add uses coverage union;
  subtract and intersect multiply soft coverage rather than thresholding it.
  Saved alpha channels use the same sparse ownership contract.
- Ellipse and lasso results retain 8-bit antialiased edges. Magic Wand produces
  binary coverage from composite RGBA byte distance. Feather, expand, contract,
  smooth, and border produce new owned masks and enter history as one selection
  command; derived outline geometry and live gesture previews remain view state.
- Selection-engine canvases are limited to 32,768 pixels per axis and
  100,000,000 pixels total. The UI limits refinement radii to 100 pixels. Its
  feather is a zero-padded square box filter, expand/contract are square
  maximum/minimum morphology, smooth is a square median, and border is expanded
  coverage minus contracted coverage; these are deterministic foundations, not
  a professional Select and Mask/refine-edge model.
- Pixel, shape, text, smart-object, group, and adjustment raster masks own
  immutable sparse 8-bit coverage stores. Their enabled state and normalized density are nondestructive
  layer properties; painting a structured layer mask never rasterizes its source.
- Mask painting applies immutable bounded coverage patches and never rewrites
  the owning layer's RGBA buffer. Pixel/mask targeting is transient UI state.
- Every layer owns a validated blend mode, independent opacity/fill opacity,
  clipping flag, and transparency/pixel/position/all lock set. Pixel locks reject
  raster and mask mutation; transparency locks preserve existing alpha during
  pixel patches; position locks reject affine edits; all locks reject property
  edits. Groups additionally choose pass-through or isolated compositing.
- Adjustment layers own a typed Brightness/Contrast, Levels, Hue/Saturation, or
  Invert payload. Their optional raster mask is canvas-sized document-space
  coverage; parameters and masks remain editable and never rewrite underlying
  pixel layers.
- Shape layers own validated rectangle, ellipse, or arbitrary path geometry and
  editable fill, stroke, stroke width, and rectangle cor

ner radius. Paths own
  ordered move, line, cubic Bézier, and close commands with finite anchors and
  controls, bounded to 10,000 commands. Text layers own multiline
  content, a fixed layout box, and validated family, size, weight, italic,
  line-height, alignment, and color style data. Both remain structured rather
  than storing cached pixels and may carry a layer-local raster mask.
- Renderable layers own an ordered list of validated color-overlay, outside-
  stroke, and drop-shadow effects. Effect enabled state, opacity, color, blend
  mode, size, offsets, and blur are canonical editable data; source pixels and
  structured payloads are never baked when an effect changes.

{"content":"# Architecture

## Status

FreetoShop is a browser-only, local-first editor under phased development. Its
npm workspaces are `apps/web`, `packages/core-document`,
`packages/command-history`, `packages/compositor`, `packages/renderer`, `packages/raster-engine`,
`packages/selection-engine`, `packages/filter-engine`,
`packages/transform-engine`, `packages/text-engine`, `packages/file-codecs`, `packages/persistence`, and
`packages/benchmarks`, and `packages/pixel-storage`.
The concrete source tree and tests are the authority when this document and code
disagree.

## Boundaries

- **`apps/web`:** owns interaction, accessibility, PWA behavior, and view
  state. Components should not encode file formats or pixel algorithms. The
  application shell delegates dialog lifecycle to `components/`, filter-command
  adaptation to `editor/filterOperations`, shared interaction contracts to
  `editor/types`, and pure document/geometry helpers to `editor/model`; new
  editor behavior must extend these boundaries instead of growing `App.tsx`.
  `workers/` is the browser-process boundary for long-running local operations:
  it owns typed request/result protocols, progress delivery, cancellation by
  worker termination, and error normalization while delegating algorithms to
  headless packages.
- **`core-document`:** owns serializable editor state, layer ordering, stable
  identifiers, invertible affine layer transforms, validated edits, and
  canonical editable shape geometry/styles, owned line/cubic vector-path
  commands, and text content/styles. It also owns
  ordered typed layer effects, their validated nondestructive parameters, owned
  embedded smart-object source trees, ordered typed smart-filter state, and
  nondestructive canvas geometry. Crop and Canvas Size change canvas bounds,
  translate only root-layer world placement, and remap canvas-sized
  selection/channel data without trimming layer-local pixels or masks. Reveal
  All derives a safe expanded rectangle from nested transformed renderable-layer
  bounds and uses the same path.
  Pixel layers canonically own immutable sparse `TiledPixelStore` resources;
  patches replace only changed tiles and history may safely share unchanged
  resources. Raster masks use the corresponding one-channel
  `TiledCoverageStore` and copy-on-write mask patches.
- **`command-history`:** applies undoable commands and owns undo/redo history.
- **`compositor`:** owns DOM-free premultiplied-alpha source-over equations, 20
  separable and six RGB-vector professional blend modes, and immutable/in-place
  same-sized surface composition. The renderer test suite keeps its mode list
  synchronized with the canonical document contract.
- **`renderer`:** turns a document and viewport into Canvas 2D pixels. Rendering must not
  mutate the document. It rasterizes affine pixel, rectangle/ellipse/path, and
  structured text layers, resolves clipping and
  group isolation, rasterizes local and document-space raster/vector masks (including
  masks over combined pass-through and isolated group results), recursively composites

smart objects, applies their
  filter-engine-backed smart filters before outer masks/effects, applies
  adjustment layers and layer effects, and delegates blend math to the compositor.
- **`raster-engine`:** owns deterministic, DOM-free pixel and mask operations.
  Brush, eraser, and adjustments consume document-space selection coverage and
  inverse-map affine coordinates, and return minimal layer-local RGBA or
  one-channel coverage patches. The same mask stroke path edits pixel, shape,
  text, and smart-object masks through their nested world transforms and group
  masks directly in document space. Image Size uses its nearest-neighbor and
  bilinear pixel-center resamplers for pixel layers, layer masks, selections,
  and channels; bilinear RGBA interpolation is performed in premultiplied alpha.
- **`selection-engine`:** creates and refines owned, canvas-sized 8-bit coverage
  masks. It owns supersampled ellipse/polygon rasterization, RMS-color Magic
  Wand matching, and deterministic mask morphology; it does not depend on the
  DOM or renderer.
- **`filter-engine`:** returns bounded immutable pixel patches for destructive
  color and Gaussian operations. It maps document-space selection coverage
  through the supplied layer world transform and leaves command/history policy
  to the caller. The renderer also reuses its Gaussian implementation for
  nondestructive smart-object intermediate surfaces.
- **`transform-engine`:** owns DOM-free transform snapshots, local/document
  handle geometry, nested-parent-aware scaling, rotation, translation, and
  singularity protection. The web app owns pointer capture, previews, and
  accessible controls. The web app likewise projects editable path anchors and
  cubic controls through nested world transforms, while core-document remains
  the canonical geometry and matrix authority.
- **`text-engine`:** lazily loads HarfBuzz WebAssembly, owns bounded local-font
  registration, OpenType substitution/positioning, direction inference, line
  layout, and positioned glyph outlines. The renderer consumes those outlines;
  system fonts without available binaries use an explicit Canvas fallback. See
  [TEXT_ENGINE.md](TEXT_ENGINE.md).
- **`file-codecs`:** translates PNG/JPEG bytes to or from the document model and
  performs bounded, import-only PSD translation through `ag-psd`. PSD parsing
  validates the binary header before decode and returns an explicit compatibility
  report; it does not leak `ag-psd` objects into canonical state. Imported data
  is untrusted.
- **`persistence`:** saves/restores supported state in IndexedDB. No server is
  required and document contents should not leave the device implicitly. It
  also owns the versioned `.freetoshop` binary container, schema migration,
  SHA-256 integrity verification, and canonical native-file decoding. See
  [NATIVE_FORMAT.md](NATIVE_FORMAT.md).
- **`benchmarks`:** builds versioned synthetic documents and enforces broad,
  CI-safe ceilings for compositor time, brush latency, and typed-array storage
  amplification. Production packages must never depend on it.
- **`pixel-storage`:*

* owns sparse immutable tile stores, copy-on-write pixel
  patches, sparse one-channel coverage stores, contiguous and tiled
  `PixelSource` adapters, owned region reads,
  chunk iteration, validated deterministic worker/persistence snapshots, and
  clipped/coalesced dirty-region accumulation. It has no dependency on the
  document model or renderer. See
  [TILED_RENDERING.md](TILED_RENDERING.md) for the staged integration contract.

{"content":"# Document Model

Pixel layers canonically own immutable sparse `TiledPixelStore` resources.
Pixel patches use copy-on-write tiles, so history versions may share unchanged
tiles without exposing mutable RGBA buffers. Contiguous materialization is an
explicit compatibility operation at legacy filter, resize, codec, export, or
version-1 persistence boundaries. Raster masks, selections, and saved alpha
channels own immutable sparse one-channel `TiledCoverageStore` resources only;
there is no dual contiguous ownership field. Coverage stores carry an implicit
8-bit default plus sparse deviation tiles, so partial selection and raster-mask
complements remain sparse through inversion, crop, resize, worker transport,
native persistence, and selection refinement. Feather, square maximum/minimum,
median smooth, and border refinement process only deviation-tile neighborhoods
plus the finite-canvas edge bands required by zero-outside semantics. Some
filter sampling paths still densify at documented algorithm boundaries. Affine selection-to-raster-mask baking reads only active
selection tiles and writes a bounded sparse destination rather than allocating
a full layer-sized coverage buffer. Sparse selection combine also reconciles
different source tile sizes on one bounded output grid without materializing
either full canvas. The
complete ownership contract is specified in
[TILED_RENDERING.md](TILED_RENDERING.md).

The cold-composite worker keeps an isolated registry of immutable tiled
resources. Version-1 task envelopes upload each pixel/coverage snapshot once per
store and snapshot scope, then use resource references for later metadata-only
document revisions. Version-2 delta envelopes derive the next immutable store
from its retained predecessor, transferring only COW tiles whose buffer identity
changed and listing removed tile keys without a payload. A task carries its live
resource set so superseded stores are evicted on both sides. Abort terminates the
worker and discards the namespace; it never reuses references or delta bases
across cancellation. Filter, resize, and native-export operations share stable
document resource slots in one sequential session. Resize, PSD-import, and
native-import results use collision-safe request-scoped resource IDs; the worker
retains owned clones before transferring buffers, and the client adopts hydrated
stores under those same IDs for zero-upload follow-up tasks.

The document model is the canonical, serializable description of an edit. A
document has a version, canvas dimensions, ordered layers, and stable IDs.
Renderable layers refer to image resources rather than DOM or canvas objects.
Viewport zoom, pan, selection chrome, dialogs, and hover state are transient UI
state. The full-resolution selection mask is document state because raster
commands, masks, and adjustments consume its 8-bit coverage.
Free Transform snapshots, active handles, pointer positions, and live previews
are also transient; only the final validated affine matrix enters document
history and persistence. Crop drafts are likewise transient; an applied crop is\

r
represented by new canvas dimensions, translated root transforms, and remapped
canvas-sized coverage buffers.

## Invariants

- Dimensions, coordinates, opacity, and resource sizes are finite and bounded.
- Layer IDs are unique within a document; layer order is deterministic.
- Unsupported layer kinds or enum values fail validation rather than being
  executed or silently reinterpreted.
- Edits are expressed as commands or equivalent pure state transitions so they
  can be tested and later support undo/redo.
- Saved documents contain data, never executable JavaScript.
- Every layer owns an invertible Canvas-style affine matrix (`a` through `f`).
  Nested world transforms compose parent × child, supporting translation,
  rotation, scale, reflection, and shear without rewriting source pixels.
- A selection is either `null` (all pixels) or an owned canvas-sized sparse
  `TiledCoverageStore`. Rectangles write only dirty patches; arbitrary masks can
  replace, add, subtract, or intersect coverage. Add uses coverage union;
  subtract and intersect multiply soft coverage rather than thresholding it.
  Saved alpha channels use the same sparse ownership contract.
- Ellipse and lasso results retain 8-bit antialiased edges. Magic Wand produces
  binary coverage from composite RGBA byte distance. Feather, expand, contract,
  smooth, and border produce new owned masks and enter history as one selection
  command; derived outline geometry and live gesture previews remain view state.
- Selection-engine canvases are limited to 32,768 pixels per axis and
  100,000,000 pixels total. The UI limits refinement radii to 100 pixels. Its
  feather is a zero-padded square box filter, expand/contract are square
  maximum/minimum morphology, smooth is a square median, and border is expanded
  coverage minus contracted coverage; these are deterministic foundations, not
  a professional Select and Mask/refine-edge model.
- Pixel, shape, text, smart-object, group, and adjustment raster masks own
  immutable sparse 8-bit coverage stores. Their enabled state and normalized density are nondestructive
  layer properties; painting a structured layer mask never rasterizes its source.
- Mask painting applies immutable bounded coverage patches and never rewrites
  the owning layer's RGBA buffer. Pixel/mask targeting is transient UI state.
- Every layer owns a validated blend mode, independent opacity/fill opacity,
  clipping flag, and transparency/pixel/position/all lock set. Pixel locks reject
  raster and mask mutation; transparency locks preserve existing alpha during
  pixel patches; position locks reject affine edits; all locks reject property
  edits. Groups additionally choose pass-through or isolated compositing.
- Adjustment layers own a typed Brightness/Contrast, Levels, Hue/Saturation, or
  Invert payload. Their optional raster mask is canvas-sized document-space
  coverage; parameters and masks remain editable and never rewrite underlying
  pixel layers.
- Shape layers own validated rectangle, ellipse, or arbitrary path geometry and
  editable fill, stroke, stroke width, and rectangle

corner radius. Paths own
  ordered move, line, cubic Bézier, and close commands with finite anchors and
  controls, bounded to 10,000 commands. Text layers own multiline
  content, a fixed layout box, and validated family, size, weight, italic,
  line-height, alignment, and color style data. Both remain structured rather
  than storing cached pixels and may carry a layer-local raster mask.
- Renderable layers own an ordered list of validated color-overlay, outside-
  stroke, and drop-shadow effects. Effect enabled state, opacity, color, blend
  mode, size, offsets, and blur are canonical editable data; source pixels and
  structured payloads are never baked when an effect changes.

{"content":"
Dependencies point inward: UI and adapters may call domain contracts; the
domain does not depend on React, browser DOM nodes, or a particular codec.

Selection outlines are renderer view data derived from the canonical coverage
mask. Filter dialog previews are transient documents; only Apply patches the
canonical pixel layer through command history. Neither engine introduces a new
persistence format or external dependency.

Schema-v6 compositing state remains framework-independent. The web layer only
chooses commands and displays controls; core-document validates layer properties
and adjustment payloads, persistence migrates them, and the renderer/compositor
produce display and export pixels from the same state.

Layer-tree duplicate/group/ungroup/remove/replace operations are headless core
commands. The UI owns transient multiselection. Merge and Flatten deliberately
cross the renderer boundary first to produce a full-canvas pixel layer, then use
one validated root replacement command; this keeps history atomic without
placing rendering dependencies inside core-document.

The web Magic Wand supplies the flattened document composite and enables alpha
sampling. Contiguous matching is a four-connected flood fill; disabling it
scans the full canvas. Freehand lasso points are retained after at least
0.5 document pixels of movement, closed on release, and rasterized by the same
four-times-supersampled even-odd polygon engine used by the headless API.

## Data flow

1. A user explicitly selects a local file.
2. A file adapter validates and decodes it into document state and pixel data.
3. Commands produce validated document updates. Long gestures may derive
   transient previews, but completion commits exactly one command. Crop drag
   and numeric-bound editing remain view state until Apply or Enter commits the
   crop through command history. Canvas Size and Image Size collect validated
   modal input before each commits one history operation. Image resampling and
   destructive filter application run in isolated module workers; completed
   results are rejected if the canonical document changed while work was in
   flight, and cancellation never commits a partial result.
4. The renderer derives the visible frame from document plus viewport state.
5. An explicit export serializes a supported output.

## Current non-goals

Collaboration, cloud sync, server rendering, arbitrary third-party code,
Photoshop parity, lossless round-tripping of unknown PSD data, and production
plugin or scripting ABI stability are not current guarantees. Pixel layers and
raster masks are tile-owned, but selections/channels, legacy algorithms, version-1 persistence,
and advanced composition still cross explicit contiguous boundaries. Resizing
is not high-bit-depth, profile-aware, or equipped with a dedicated
area-downsampling filter. Worker progress is currently operation-level rather
than per-tile.

{"content":"- Embedded smart-object layers own a stable source ID, source canvas, and nested
  layer tree. Conversion moves the original layer payload into an identity-
  transformed source while retaining outer placement and compositing;
  replacement swaps the source atomically and clears an incompatible outer
  mask. Nested editing uses a separate history; Save commits one source-
  replacement command to the retained parent history, while Cancel restores the
  parent without mutation. Programmatic and serialized nesting is limited to 16 levels.
- Duplicate recursively safely shares immutable pixel and raster-mask
  resources, owns mutable adjustment resources, and assigns new
  stable descendant IDs. Grouping requires common-parent layers and preserves
  their stack order. Ungrouping is limited to unclipped Normal pass-through
  groups so composing the group transform and opacity into its children does
  not silently change rendered pixels. Merge replaces selected root siblings at
  their lowest stack position; Flatten replaces all roots. Their rasterization
  is supplied by the renderer before one core tree-replacement command.
- Saved alpha channels are owned, uniquely identified, canvas-sized 8-bit
  coverage buffers. Saving and loading preserve soft coverage exactly; channel
  preview choice remains transient UI state.
- Cropping is nondestructive with respect to layer resources. It pre-multiplies
  each root transform by the inverse crop-origin translation while leaving
  nested transforms, pixel buffers, and layer-local raster masks intact.
  Explicit selection and saved-channel coverage is copied into the new canvas;
  crop area outside the old canvas receives zero coverage. An implicit `null`
  selection remains the full new canvas.
- Crop coordinates are integers, dimensions are positive, neither axis may
  exceed 32,768 pixels, and total area may not exceed 100,000,000 pixels.
- Canvas Size supports top, center, and bottom crossed with left, center, and
  right anchors. The anchor fixes the corresponding old-canvas point to a
  deterministic nearest-pixel position. Root transforms receive the resulting
  translation; nested transforms, pixel buffers, and layer-local masks remain
  unchanged. Canvas-sized selection and channel coverage is shifted, trimmed,
  or zero-padded with the canvas.
- Reveal All unions the existing canvas with the floor/ceil bounds of every
  visible, nonzero-opacity pixel layer after nested affine transforms. Hidden
  layers and zero-opacity branches do not expand it. It is deliberately
  bounds-based: transparent source pixels and mask coverage are not scanned, so
  a fully transparent or masked layer can still contribute geometric bounds.
- Image Size scales the document coordinate system, resamples every pixel layer
  and layer-local raster mask, and resamples explicit document selections and
  saved channels to the new canvas. Root transforms absorb document scaling;
  nested affine transforms remain structurally nested, while resized pixel
  layers compensate their local coordinate scale so transformed content keeps
  its proportional d

ocument placement. A `null` selection remains implicit
  full-canvas coverage.
- Canvas Size, Reveal All, and Image Size enforce the same 32,768-pixel-per-axis
  and 100,000,000-pixel canvas-area ceilings as Crop. Image Size also validates
  every resized layer allocation against those ceilings and rejects an estimated
  resize working set above 1,000,000,000 bytes.
- Destructive filters are not document objects. They return a minimal changed
  rectangle whose RGBA bytes replace part of one pixel layer in one history
  step. Cancelled live previews and filter parameters are transient and are not
  persisted. Color filters retain source alpha; Gaussian Blur may blur alpha and
  blends its result through soft selection coverage in premultiplied space.
- Filter output is capped at 512 MiB. Gaussian radius is an integer from 0
  through 100; its estimated Float32 convolution buffer plus source bytes is
  separately capped at 512 MiB. Operations are synchronous CPU passes over the
  selected pixel layer; they neither bake nor modify its separate raster mask.

The current model supports affine-transformed pixel/group, shape, and text layers,
full-resolution selections, raster masks and editable vector masks, saved alpha channels,
nondestructive canvas geometry operations, and destructive raster Image Size
resampling. It also supports arbitrary raster selections and destructive pixel
filter patches, 26 deterministic professional blend modes, clipping, isolated
groups, layer locks, four typed nondestructive adjustment layers, editable vector
paths, three editable layer effects, embedded smart objects, and ordered smart-filter stacks. Smart
filters have stable IDs, enabled state, opacity, and validated type-specific
parameters; filter IDs are unique within their owning smart object. Vector masks
on pixel, shape, text, smart-object, adjustment, and group layers own bounded
move/line/cubic/close commands plus enabled, density, and inversion state; they
combine multiplicatively with raster masks. Group raster and vector masks are canvas-sized and
constrain the group's combined pass-through or isolated result. Smart-filter masks/blend options, linked/shared smart-object
instances, embedded-font persistence, mixed-direction bidi text, Boolean path operations, Dissolve,
broader layer effects, and knockout behavior remain
reserved concepts unless tests and UI demonstrate otherwise.

Persistence schema v16 stores affine transforms, selections, raster masks, saved
alpha channels, layer compositing properties and locks, group isolation, and
typed adjustment, shape, text, and embedded smart-object layers plus editable
effects and smart filters. It explicitly migrates v1 snapshots with identity
transforms, schemas v2–v4 from legacy `{x,y}` translations, and schema v5 with
safe Normal/pass-through/unlocked defaults, plus schema v6 documents without
structured layers, schema v7 layers with an empty effects list, schema v8
documents with no smart objects, schema v9 smart objects with empty filter
stacks, schema v10 documents with the original blend-mode set, and schema v11
shape geometry with empty pat

h-command lists, and schema v12 pixel layers with
no vector mask, schema v13 structured/adjustment layers with no vector mask, and
schema v14 groups with no vector mask, and schema v15 groups with no raster mask.
Future evolution
must follow the same migration rule. Crop requires no schema revision because
schema v16 already stores every changed field; recovery stores the applied
result, not transient dialog/draft state or the undo stack. Canvas Size, Reveal
All, and Image Size likewise require no schema change because their applied
canvas, transforms, raster resources, masks, selections, and channels already
belong to schema v16.
See [FILE_FORMATS.md](FILE_FORMATS.md).
","role":"tool","tool_call_id":"call_740843ed89484ea5b61b28ad"}

{"content":"# Architecture

## Status

FreetoShop is a browser-only, local-first editor under phased development. Its
npm workspaces are `apps/web`, `packages/core-document`,
`packages/command-history`, `packages/compositor`, `packages/renderer`, `packages/raster-engine`,
`packages/selection-engine`, `packages/filter-engine`,
`packages/transform-engine`, `packages/text-engine`, `packages/file-codecs`, `packages/persistence`, and
`packages/benchmarks`, and `packages/pixel-storage`.
The concrete source tree and tests are the authority when this document and code
disagree.

## Boundaries

- **`apps/web`:** owns interaction, accessibility, PWA behavior, and view
  state. Components should not encode file formats or pixel algorithms. The
  application shell delegates dialog lifecycle to `components/`, filter-command
  adaptation to `editor/filterOperations`, shared interaction contracts to
  `editor/types`, and pure document/geometry helpers to `editor/model`; new
  editor behavior must extend these boundaries instead of growing `App.tsx`.
  `workers/` is the browser-process boundary for long-running local operations:
  it owns typed request/result protocols, progress delivery, cancellation by
  worker termination, and error normalization while delegating algorithms to
  headless packages.
- **`core-document`:** owns serializable editor state, layer ordering, stable
  identifiers, invertible affine layer transforms, validated edits, and
  canonical editable shape geometry/styles, owned line/cubic vector-path
  commands, and text content/styles. It also owns
  ordered typed layer effects, their validated nondestructive parameters, owned
  embedded smart-object source trees, ordered typed smart-filter state, and
  nondestructive canvas geometry. Crop and Canvas Size change canvas bounds,
  translate only root-layer world placement, and remap canvas-sized
  selection/channel data without trimming layer-local pixels or masks. Reveal
  All derives a safe expanded rectangle from nested transformed renderable-layer
  bounds and uses the same path.
  Pixel layers canonically own immutable sparse `TiledPixelStore` resources;
  patches replace only changed tiles and history may safely share unchanged
  resources. Raster masks use the corresponding one-channel
  `TiledCoverageStore` and copy-on-write mask patches.
- **`command-history`:** applies undoable commands and owns undo/redo history.
- **`compositor`:** owns DOM-free premultiplied-alpha source-over equations, 20
  separable and six RGB-vector professional blend modes, and immutable/in-place
  same-sized surface composition. The renderer test suite keeps its mode list
  synchronized with the canonical document contract.
- **`renderer`:** turns a document and viewport into Canvas 2D pixels. Rendering must not
  mutate the document. It rasterizes affine pixel, rectangle/ellipse/path, and
  structured text layers, resolves clipping and
  group isolation, rasterizes local and document-space raster/vector masks (including
  masks over combined pass-through and isolated group results), recursively composites

smart objects, applies their
  filter-engine-backed smart filters before outer masks/effects, applies
  adjustment layers and layer effects, and delegates blend math to the compositor.
- **`raster-engine`:** owns deterministic, DOM-free pixel and mask operations.
  Brush, eraser, and adjustments consume document-space selection coverage and
  inverse-map affine coordinates, and return minimal layer-local RGBA or
  one-channel coverage patches. The same mask stroke path edits pixel, shape,
  text, and smart-object masks through their nested world transforms and group
  masks directly in document space. Image Size uses its nearest-neighbor and
  bilinear pixel-center resamplers for pixel layers, layer masks, selections,
  and channels; bilinear RGBA interpolation is performed in premultiplied alpha.
- **`selection-engine`:** creates and refines owned, canvas-sized 8-bit coverage
  masks. It owns supersampled ellipse/polygon rasterization, RMS-color Magic
  Wand matching, and deterministic mask morphology; it does not depend on the
  DOM or renderer.
- **`filter-engine`:** returns bounded immutable pixel patches for destructive
  color and Gaussian operations. It maps document-space selection coverage
  through the supplied layer world transform and leaves command/history policy
  to the caller. The renderer also reuses its Gaussian implementation for
  nondestructive smart-object intermediate surfaces.
- **`transform-engine`:** owns DOM-free transform snapshots, local/document
  handle geometry, nested-parent-aware scaling, rotation, translation, and
  singularity protection. The web app owns pointer capture, previews, and
  accessible controls. The web app likewise projects editable path anchors and
  cubic controls through nested world transforms, while core-document remains
  the canonical geometry and matrix authority.
- **`text-engine`:** lazily loads HarfBuzz WebAssembly, owns bounded local-font
  registration, OpenType substitution/positioning, direction inference, line
  layout, and positioned glyph outlines. The renderer consumes those outlines;
  system fonts without available binaries use an explicit Canvas fallback. See
  [TEXT_ENGINE.md](TEXT_ENGINE.md).
- **`file-codecs`:** translates PNG/JPEG bytes to or from the document model and
  performs bounded, import-only PSD translation through `ag-psd`. PSD parsing
  validates the binary header before decode and returns an explicit compatibility
  report; it does not leak `ag-psd` objects into canonical state. Imported data
  is untrusted.
- **`persistence`:** saves/restores supported state in IndexedDB. No server is
  required and document contents should not leave the device implicitly. It
  also owns the versioned `.freetoshop` binary container, schema migration,
  SHA-256 integrity verification, and canonical native-file decoding. See
  [NATIVE_FORMAT.md](NATIVE_FORMAT.md).
- **`benchmarks`:** builds versioned synthetic documents and enforces broad,
  CI-safe ceilings for compositor time, brush latency, and typed-array storage
  amplification. Production packages must never depend on it.
- **`pixel-storage`:*

* owns sparse immutable tile stores, copy-on-write pixel
  patches, sparse one-channel coverage stores, contiguous and tiled
  `PixelSource` adapters, owned region reads,
  chunk iteration, validated deterministic worker/persistence snapshots, and
  clipped/coalesced dirty-region accumulation. It has no dependency on the
  document model or renderer. See
  [TILED_RENDERING.md](TILED_RENDERING.md) for the staged integration contract.
